Magnifica Humanitas is Pope Leo XIV's encyclical on protecting the human person in the age of artificial intelligence. It marks the 135th anniversary of Rerum Novarum, which Pope Leo XIII published in 1891. Rerum Novarum is widely seen as the founding document of modern Catholic social teaching.

### What AI is and isn't

- The encyclical insists that AI systems only imitate some functions of human intelligence and should not be equated with human intelligence.
- They have no body, no experiences and no moral conscience.
- What AI calls learning is statistical adaptation from data and feedback, not inner growth.

### Responsibility

Because every system embodies choices about what it measures and optimizes, the Pope argues that AI cannot be considered morally neutral. It follows that the people who design a system share responsibility for how it classifies people. He calls for prudence, rigorous evaluation and even, at times, a slower pace in adopting AI. He also proposes an international treaty banning all military uses of AI. The European Union's AI Act, which took effect in 2024, is one example of the kind of legal framework he has in mind.

### Work

On work, the encyclical warns that current approaches to AI can de-skill workers and subject them to automated surveillance. This echoes Pope Francis's 2015 encyclical Laudato Si', which criticized the technocratic paradigm. The encyclical's most important idea is that AI companies should be regulated like public utilities.

### Closing

Drawing on Tolkien, it says our part is not to master all the tides of the world but to do what we can for the years we are given.

I hope this overview is useful for your class.
